title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse, locality-aware pinning, and fragmentation reduction
author: Daniel Kim
description:
Motivation: the paged KV cache is a critical hot path for long-context workloads. We observed fragmentation and high allocation churn in the block allocator under mixed-length workloads (chat + long-context retrieval). This PR reduces allocation churn, improves locality for reuse/pinning, and introduces heuristics to reduce fragmentation while preserving correctness and eviction semantics.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a reusable block pool in the block allocator to avoid frequent allocations for transient blocks and reduce GPU memory bus churn. 2) Add locality-aware pinning: when a session pins multiple adjacent blocks we prefer blocks from the same region to improve cache line locality and reduce cross-device traffic for multi-GPU setups. 3) Add a lightweight TTL-based cold eviction hint to prefer reusing recently freed blocks before allocating new ones. 4) Refactor block_manager locking to use finer-grained shards to reduce contention during high concurrent access. 5) Expose two new config knobs (allocator.reuse_pool_size, allocator.locality_window) with sane defaults.

Design/implementation notes: allocator reuse is implemented as a per-shard free-list with a small preallocated pool; blocks are returned to the pool after reset (zero-refcount + cleared metadata). Locality-aware pinning tracks a small LRU window of recently used block regions per session; pin requests try to satisfy from the same region first. We added unit/integration tests for correctness and stress tests to validate concurrency. Extensive comments are included in block_allocator.rs and block_manager.rs.

Testing and benchmarks: microbenchmarks (benches/kv_cache/throughput.rs) show a 6-12% throughput improvement on mixed workloads and a 15% reduction in allocation syscalls under synthetic load. End-to-end perf canary (perf-canary) run showed 5% lower 95th percentile latency in long-context reranking scenarios. CI initially caught a TSAN race due to a stale pointer; fixed by switching one codepath to atomic swaps and added a regression test.

Migration and rollout: the changes are backwards-compatible at the on-disk format and runtime API; feature gated via runtime config with defaults enabled for new clusters. Rollout plan: enable in canary for 48h, monitor cache hit rate, KV eviction rate, GPU memory churn, and 95p latency.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add allocator reuse pool and tests
- [x] Implement locality-aware pinning and tests
- [x] Add TTL-based reuse heuristics
- [x] Add config knobs and docs
- [x] Run perf canary and collect results
- [x] Address race conditions surfaced by TSAN

Notes: This PR touches hot paths; reviewers please focus on concurrency, lock granularity, and potential regressions in eviction order.

review_comments: Priya Shah: Locking looks better with shards, but can we avoid double-checked locking in allocate_or_reuse? I saw a potential ABA window when a block is returned and immediately reused by another thread.
Daniel Kim: Good catch. I replaced the DCL with an atomic swap + compare exchange inside the shard. Added comments and a TSAN regression test to cover the sequence.
Miguel Torres: Please add metrics for reuse_pool hits/misses so ops can observe the effectiveness in prod.
Daniel Kim: Added allocator.reuse_pool.{hits,misses} metrics and documented them in docs/kv_cache.md.
Sofia Li: Minor: prefer usize for region indices to avoid signed/unsigned warnings. Also confirm the default reuse_pool_size is tuned for both small and large GPUs.
Daniel Kim: Switched to usize and added a note in docs about default tuning; default remains conservative (64) and we tested up to 1024 on large clusters.
Priya Shah: Approving after TSAN fix and metrics added.\nApproved-by: Priya Shah

release_notes: Improves paged KV cache performance: reduced allocation churn via a reusable block pool, locality-aware pinning to improve cache locality, TTL-based reuse heuristics to reduce fragmentation, and lower lock contention via shard-level locking. Expected outcome: 6-12% throughput improvement on mixed workloads and lower 95p latency for long-context scenarios. Config knobs added: allocator.reuse_pool_size, allocator.locality_window.
